before: Assay distinction. A predicted binding IC50 estimates a competitive-binding assay endpoint. An IC50 depends on the assay conditions and is not automatically an equilibrium dissociation constant. Cer and colleagues' 2009 IC50-to-Ki tool calculates binding or inhibition constants using the interaction mechanism, concentrations and other assumptions; this is a biochemical distinction, not validation of an HLA model or a measure of cancer-cell growth inhibition. Reading guide (OnCo inference): Record the model and version, allele, peptide length, prediction task, units, reference distribution and threshold beside every score, and do not put a rank and an IC50 in one unlabelled column. A threshold is a selection rule for a stated workflow and cannot repair the wrong allele or an unsupported task. Inputs are peptide or source-protein sequences and an exact allele; scoring uses no tumour tissue; held-out validation, allele coverage and the endpoint (binding, recovery or T-cell recognition) decide what a good score means.

Output table in words. Predicted binding IC50 in nanomolar units: lower values mean stronger predicted competitive binding for that output, and it is not a measured concentration, an equilibrium dissociation constant or a functional T-cell response.
